title: Some Things I Like about 5 Games I Don't Like
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9rVcXaVHCXw

Daniel (@dungeondive) does not enjoy making negative reviews, so this is the compromise: five games he genuinely dislikes, each one paired with the thing about it he admires. Nearly all of them, he notes, would sit in the top ten of somebody who likes exactly the games he likes. The list is ordered by rehabilitation prospects — number five he would not take for free, number one he would buy again tomorrow.

*Middara* loses him to sheer volume of prose ("I don't want to read a novel while I am playing a game"), but the maps that rearrange themselves mid-quest — a wall crumbling, a fall to a level you had not been told existed — produced real surprise at the table. *Final Girl* is the only board game he has ever rage-quit, three learning games in and straight to the game store to sell it; the modular map-plus-slasher-plus-heroine assembly is nonetheless tailor-made for him. *Sword & Sorcery* suffers from anachronistic humour and level-ups where neither choice excites, yet its enemy AI makes a limited bestiary feel large. *Gloomhaven* he calls a dungeon crawl for people who don't like dungeon crawls; what he admires is the value of that first Kickstarter.

The number one is *Mage Knight*, which strips out drama by letting you calculate the outcome before you commit — an accountant weighing risk rather than a hero taking it. He loves how it looks on the table, and he might yet come around.

----

Is there a game you've bounced off hard that you can still name one genuinely great thing about?
